verdict.summary: You can create an app and install it in your own workspace in minutes, and unlisted distribution needs no review. Commercial use effectively needs Marketplace review (up to about 10 business days plus 10 weeks), and unlisted apps get tight rate limits on history methods.
verdict.hands_on_effort: 1-2 days for Gate 1-2; several more days to prepare a Marketplace submission
verdict.approval_wait: None for unlisted installs; Marketplace review up to 10 business days (preliminary) plus up to 10 weeks (functional) for new apps

gates.name: Unpublished app in its own workspace
gates.unlocks: Install the app in the workspace that owns it and connect your own account.
limits: A new app can only be installed in its associated workspace until distribution is activated.

gates.name: Unlisted public distribution
gates.unlocks: Any workspace can install through the Add to Slack button or shareable install URL, with no Slack review. Slack frames this as for pilots.
limits: 1 request per minute and 15 objects per request on conversations.history and conversations.replies for unlisted commercially distributed apps (applied to existing installs from March 3, 2026).
Some workspaces allow only admin-approved or only Marketplace-listed apps.
Slack's terms say the Marketplace is the only appropriate channel for commercial distribution.
No numeric install cap was found.
gates.time_to_reach: About 1 hour after Gate 1, once HTTPS redirect URLs are set

gates.name: Slack Marketplace listing
gates.unlocks: Marketplace approval removes the unlisted rate limits and allows installs in Marketplace-only workspaces. Slack does not charge for inclusion.
limits: At least 10 installs on active workspaces, held through the whole review.
Preliminary review up to 10 business days; functional review up to 10 weeks (6 weeks for resubmissions of published apps).
Scope or config changes after publishing need re-review.

steps.title: Sign in and create the app
steps.detail: Go to the Slack app management page, sign in to Slack, and create a new app in a workspace you control. Use a current (non-classic) app.
gotchas: Account prerequisites such as plan or Developer Program enrollment were not confirmed.

steps.title: Add the Composio redirect URI
steps.detail: In the app's OAuth & Permissions settings, add the callback URL from your Composio auth config under Redirect URLs. It must be HTTPS, with no anchor.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

gotchas: With multiple Redirect URLs, redirect_uri must be sent in both the authorize and access steps, or Slack returns bad_redirect_uri.
Redirect URL edits take effect immediately.

steps.title: Choose a minimal scope set
steps.detail: Draft the smallest bot scopes (and user scopes only if the app acts as the authorizing user) with a one-line reason per scope. Avoid Composio's broad defaults such as *:history and search:read.* unless you need them. Consider marking some scopes optional in the manifest.
gotchas: Bot scopes and user scopes go in different parameters: scope and user_scope.
Scopes are additive and cannot be removed from a token without revoking it.

steps.title: Put your client ID and secret into Composio and connect
steps.detail: Copy the Client ID and Client Secret from Basic Information into a Composio custom auth config for the slack toolkit, then authorize your own workspace.
gotchas: Slack tokens do not expire by default. Token rotation and PKCE are opt-in, and once enabled they cannot be turned off.

steps.title: Activate public distribution
steps.detail: Under Manage Distribution, complete the checklist (HTTPS redirect URLs, etc.) and click Activate Public Distribution. This gives you an Add to Slack button and a shareable install URL.
gotchas: Adding scopes later means existing installs must reinstall.
Admin-restricted workspaces may block unlisted apps.

steps.title: Plan around unlisted rate limits
steps.detail: If your agent reads channel history, expect 1 request per minute on conversations.history and conversations.replies until Marketplace approval. Decide whether to pursue the Marketplace.

steps.title: Reach 10 active installs
steps.detail: Marketplace submission requires at least 10 installs on active workspaces, and the count must hold through review. Use unlisted distribution to get there.

steps.title: Prepare submission assets
steps.detail: Draft the privacy policy, landing page, scope justifications, and support channel. The privacy policy must cover data collected, use, retention, and deletion requests, with a contact email or web form. Prepare a 1600x1000 image and a 30-90 second demo video on public YouTube. Also prepare a demo video showing install, OAuth, and uninstall.
gotchas: Support must respond within 2 business days.
Reviewers cannot use any Slack workspace; provide a way for them to install without one, plus test credentials for any third-party service.

steps.title: Submit for Marketplace review
steps.detail: Submit from your app's settings. The preliminary stage takes up to 10 business days and the functional stage up to 10 weeks.
gotchas: Resubmitting during the preliminary stage resets your queue place.

steps.title: Wait for review and respond to feedback
steps.detail: Answer reviewer questions on scopes. Broad scopes trigger enhanced review, and admin.* scopes are unlikely to be approved outside the partner program.

steps.title: Maintain a staging app
steps.detail: After publishing, scope or config changes need re-review. Keep a staging app identical to the published one for substantial changes.

requirements.detail: SSL is required for OAuth redirect and interaction URLs on apps opened to other workspaces. Redirect_uri must match a configured Redirect URL.

requirements.item: Installable production-ready app with demo video and reviewer access
requirements.detail: Demo video of install, OAuth, and uninstall. Reviewers need to install without their own workspace, and test credentials for any third-party service.

requirements.item: Privacy policy, landing page, support channel, listing image and video
requirements.detail: Privacy policy states collection, use, retention, and deletion requests. Support responds within 2 business days.
Must hold through the whole review.
User-token scopes are accepted only when the app acts as its authenticating user. Unnecessary use gets the submission returned.

scopes.effect: Part of Composio's default scope set. Slack's docs sort scopes into always-allowed, requires-approval, and restricted groups. This one was not specifically categorized in the findings.
Enhanced review. Slack is unlikely to approve broad user-scope history without a clear use case. Also tied to the unlisted rate limits.
Enhanced review. Slack lists search:read among scopes unsuitable for the Marketplace without a use case.
Unlikely to be approved for apps outside Slack's partner program.
Installing a published app with unapproved scopes returns unapproved_scope. Non-existent or conflicting scopes return invalid_scope.

blockers.symptom: conversations.history returns rate-limit errors at more than 1 request per minute
blockers.cause: Unlisted commercially distributed apps are limited, with a 15-object cap per request.
blockers.fix: Get Marketplace approval, or reduce reliance on history calls.

blockers.cause: The scopes were never approved or are still in review for a published app.
blockers.fix: Wait for approval or request only approved scopes.

blockers.cause: redirect_uri is not HTTPS, does not match a configured Redirect URL, or is missing from one step when multiple URLs are set.
blockers.fix: Send identical redirect_uri in both authorize and access steps and match the configured URL.

blockers.cause: Workspace allows only approved or Marketplace-listed apps.
blockers.fix: Ask the admin to approve, or get Marketplace listing.

blockers.cause: Broad or unnecessary user-token scopes without justification.
blockers.fix: Trim scopes and give a reason for each.

composio.note: Start on Composio's managed Slack app to prototype. Its default scopes are broad and include history and search scopes that Slack's review treats as enhanced-review or unsuitable. For wide distribution or a Marketplace listing, register your own Slack app with a scope set you can justify. Composio's catalog default redirect is https://backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add, but a probe used a different callback path, so use the exact URL shown in your Composio auth config.

open_questions: Account prerequisites (free developer account, Developer Program, paid plan, org admin, business verification) were not confirmed.

Which Composio redirect URI applies to a custom Slack app: the catalog says https://backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add, a probe used https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback. Use the one in your Composio auth config.
No numeric install cap for unlisted apps was found.
Current review queue estimates shown in app settings were not checked (needs login).
Whether Composio-managed Slack auth can back a Marketplace-listed product was not verified.
Client_id validation behavior at the authorize endpoint was not confirmed by probe.
